data_section_full_text:
3.1 Sample selection

In the post-SFAS 130 period, comprehensive income disclosures are not yet fully
reported in Compustat or any other machine-readable database. <sup>11</sup> Therefore, to
manage our data collection efforts we selected a smaller but still representative
sample of U.S. firms: the firms included in the S&P 500 index. For these firms we
hand-collected reported total comprehensive income and OCI component data from
annual 10-K reports that were filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission
(SEC) over the years 1998 through 2003. For the S&P 500 firms over the years 1994
through 1997 (before SFAS 130) and 1998 through 2003 (after SFAS 130) we also
calculate the three as-if components of OCI as described in Dhaliwal et al. (1999).
Thus our sample period spans ten years: four years before and six years after the
introduction of SFAS 130. Our data set consists of six years of post-SFAS 130 asreported OCI data and ten years, both pre- and post-SFAS 130, of as-if OCI data.
Other financial statement data, required for the analysis, are obtained from
Compustat. Stock prices and returns are obtained from the Center of Research in
Security Prices (CRSP) database.
